name: Sliding Sands Trail (Keonehe'ehe'e)
why: Down a path of red and black cinders into the summit crater of Haleakala, among cinder cones and silverswords, at 3,000 m.
book: No permit for day hikes. Park entrance fee. A reservation is needed only to drive up for sunrise (recreation.gov).
dangers: The way back is all uphill at 3,000 m: count twice the time.
Cold, wind and fog at the top; strong sun.
Altitude: go slowly if you came up from the beach the same day.
turnaround: Turn back at Ka Lu'u o ka O'o or after half your time.

points.name: Ka Lu'u o ka O'o
points.note: A red cinder cone on the crater floor; the trail goes round its rim.
